title: terraform-storage-module-kms-guardrails-rotation-and-snapshot-retention
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Private deployments require consistent, secure defaults for block and file storage plus object buckets. Current customer onboarding has produced multiple manual configuration steps for KMS keys, key rotation, and snapshot retention leading to inconsistent security posture and accidental high-cost snapshot retention.

Goal: Deliver a Terraform storage module update that enforces KMS guardrails (default CMKs, key rotation enablement, explicit aliasing), sane snapshot lifecycle defaults for EBS/EFS, and bucket lifecycle policies for S3. Provide a migration plan, health checks, and an upgrade path that minimizes downtime for existing Private customers.

Scope:
- Terraform module variables and validation for kms_key_id, kms_key_alias, enable_rotation (default true).
- Module-level enforcement of server-side encryption defaults for EBS, EFS, and S3 when customers do not override explicitly.
- Snapshot lifecycle: default retention 30 days, configurable via variable with minimum 7 days validation.
- S3 lifecycle: transition to infrequent access at 30 days, delete after 365 days by default.
- Health checks: Terraform-created AWS Config rules or CloudWatch metrics + a lightweight Lambda probe to validate encryption and snapshot retention policies are in effect post-deploy.
- Migration: automated import plan using terraform import guidance and a mitigated rollout (canary + account-level rollout script).

Out of scope: full UI Console changes and Dedicated reserved-capacity specific logic (handled in a follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: New module exposes variables: kms_key_id (optional), kms_key_alias (optional), enable_key_rotation (default 'true'), snapshot_retention_days (default '30'), s3_lifecycle_days_to_ia (default '30'), s3_lifecycle_days_to_delete (default '365')
Terraform plan shows server-side encryption resources only when not overridden by consumer variables
Automated test workspace (TF) demonstrates migration for an existing EBS volume imported into the module with no downtime and snapshots pruned to configured retention
Health check Lambda + CloudWatch alarm runs as part of the module and reports when any unencrypted resource or over-retained snapshot is detected
Security review sign-off completed and documented in links
Documentation updated with migration steps and an example 'canary' workspace
Module passes internal CI: fmt, validate, lint, and a small e2e apply in a sandbox account
implementation_notes: Design decisions: prefer customer-managed CMKs when provided, otherwise create a module-scoped CMK with alias 'redwood/private-storage/<env>'
Enable key rotation by default on any CMK we create. If kms_key_id is passed, validate via data lookup that rotation is enabled or warn in plan.
For EBS/EFS snapshots, implement an aws_backup_vault + lifecycle rules where available otherwise an SSM-run Lambda that prunes older snapshots based on tags.
S3 lifecycle rule using aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration with transition and expiration rules. Ensure rule IDs are stable across applies.

Health check will be small Python Lambda that lists resources in the account/region filtered by Module tags and emits metric for noncompliant resources. Expose a boolean output 'health_check_deployed'
Provide migration helper scripts in 'examples/migrations/' that run terraform import for common patterns and generate a plan showing the minimal changes required.
testing_steps: 1) Deploy new module in sandbox without providing kms_key_id -> verify TF creates CMK, alias present, rotation enabled
2) Deploy with kms_key_id pointing to pre-existing key that has rotation disabled -> expect plan warning and optional remediation steps
3) Create EBS snapshot older than snapshot_retention_days and run health check Lambda -> alarm should trigger and a remediation runbook should be linked
4) Import an existing EBS volume into the module using terraform import and run apply; verify no data plane downtime and new snapshot policy applies
5) Verify S3 lifecycle rules transition objects to IA at configured days and deletion occurs after expected threshold in a long-running sandbox
6) Run CI e2e that applies module, runs health check, and tears down resources
rollout_plan: Phase 0: ship module in canary mode for internal sandbox accounts. Phase 1: opt-in rollout for 3 pilot customers with dedicated support. Phase 2: provide migration helpers and offer assisted migration. Phase 3: enable default enforcement for new Private deployments and opt-out guidance for existing customers. Each phase runs for at least 2 weeks and includes post-deploy audit via the health-check Lambda.
updates: 2025-02-13: Initial spike completed; validated CMK creation pattern and key aliasing approach. Prototype Lambda health check built.
2025-02-18: Security reviewed high-level design; recommended explicit aliasing and tagging. Added rotation validation behavior for customer-supplied keys.
2025-02-24: Migration script prototype for terraform import reviewed by infra; needs additional idempotency checks. Planning CI sandbox e2e next.
2025-02-26: Began PR for module changes (infra#2194). Requesting review from crypto/security and infra-sre.
rollback_plan: If issues found post-deploy, revert to previous module version via terraform state rollback and restore previous CMK alias mapping. For snapshots, re-enable retention by running remediation Lambda with last-known-good retention value. Notify customers and open a rollback incident runbook.
